digest.component_or_area: Jira Reconciler – baseline advance and inbound field sync
propositions: Local status changes are silently reverted by the reconciler when the baseline snapshot lags the outbound push by one reconciliation pass, causing state-class fields to be incorrectly suppressed from outbound and overwritten by inbound.

The baseline is advanced from the pass-START snapshot before outbound mutations complete, so when rebar pushes a status to Jira, the baseline retains the old value and becomes out-of-sync with the last-synced state that ADR 0026 specifies.

The guard `local == baseline` implies 'local is unchanged since sync', but this premise is false for one pass after rebar's own outbound write, because baseline holds the pre-push value while local has been reverted by the operator to a previous value.

A reopen (local closed → open, then open → closed by reconciler) or un-claim matches the ABA pattern: the operator's correction survives into pass N+1 only to be clobbered when inbound overwrites a suppressed status field.

The defect exposes all five inbound-mirrored fields (summary, description, priority, status, assignee) because they all share the `_suppressed_by_inbound` guard and have no per-mutation success reporting to gate baseline advance.
